kind_reason: The title marks the proposal as declined and it ends with a panel summary and reviewer comments.
title: Lignin-rich flexible polyurethane foams for upholstery (proposal, declined)

aims.summary: Formulate flexible polyurethane foams with 30 % bio-content using fractionated kraft and organosolv lignin.
Relate lignin type and hydroxyl content to foaming dynamics and cell structure.
Demonstrate durability of lignin-rich foams under cyclic compression for upholstery use.

findings.summary: Preliminary foams with 15 % lignin reached a compression set below 10 %.

methods.name: SEM, compression testing and dynamic mechanical analysis
methods.detail: Analysis of foam structure and mechanical behaviour.

datasets.name: Dataset linking lignin structure to foam properties

reviewer_objections.quote: The applicants do not demonstrate that the foams meet fire-safety standard EN 13501 at the proposed bio-content.
reviewer_objections.summary: Fire-safety compliance (EN 13501) at the proposed bio-content is not shown.

reviewer_objections.quote: The durability plan lacks a comparison with commercial petroleum-based foams over at least 50,000 compression cycles.
reviewer_objections.summary: Durability is not benchmarked against commercial petroleum-based foams over 50,000 cycles.

reviewer_objections.quote: Strong science, but the application case is not yet convincing; fire behaviour and long-term durability must be addressed before funding.
reviewer_objections.summary: The panel wants fire behaviour and long-term durability addressed before funding.

open_questions.summary: Can foams with 30 % lignin bio-content pass the EN 13501 fire-safety standard?
How do lignin-rich foams compare with commercial petroleum-based foams over at least 50,000 compression cycles?
